title: State Medicaid Payment Policies for Medicare Cost Sharing (Policy in Brief)
note: As of May 2025, 41 states used lesser-of policies for physician services, 5 paid cost sharing in full and 5 used other policies.

title: 45 CFR 162.925: Additional requirements for health plans (HIPAA transactions)
note: If an entity asks a health plan to conduct a transaction as a standard transaction, the plan must do so.

title: 45 CFR 162.1602: Standards for health care electronic funds transfers and remittance advice transaction
note: Bank transfer format with the reassociation trace number that also appears on the electronic remittance.

title: Guidance letter GL-2022-04: health plans' payment of claims using virtual credit cards and the adopted standards for electronic funds transfer and remittance advice
note: Plans may pay by virtual card but must use the standard bank transfer and remittance when a provider asks, and may not require use of a vendor's services as a condition. Providers must ask their own bank to deliver the trace number.

title: Remittance Advice Remark Codes
note: MA18: claim forwarded to the supplemental insurer. MA19: not forwarded because the Medigap information was invalid. MA13: penalties for billing amounts not marked patient responsibility. MA130: unprocessable claim, no appeal rights.

title: Claim Status Codes
note: Used to check a vendor document's error code meanings: codes 4 and 5 concern requests for information, 21 is missing or invalid information.

title: Federal sequestration payment reductions
note: The 2% reduction applies to the final payment after deductible and coinsurance and is shown with reason code 253. Page dated July 7, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 149.620: Patient-provider dispute resolution process
note: A bill at least $400 above the good faith estimate is substantially in excess. The patient has 120 calendar days from the bill to start a dispute.

title: 45 CFR 149.510: Independent dispute resolution process (No Surprises Act)
note: Out-of-network commercial claims only. The arbitrator must not consider public payer rates, usual and customary charges or billed charges.

title: 45 CFR 160.103: Definitions (HIPAA), business associate
12 CFR 1026.2: Definitions and rules of construction (Truth in Lending, Regulation Z)
note: A creditor is a person who regularly extends consumer credit payable by written agreement in more than four installments, or subject to a finance charge. Regularly means more than 25 times in the prior year.

title: 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7k(d): Reporting and returning of overpayments
note: Covers funds received under Medicare or Medicaid. Deadline is 60 days after the overpayment is identified. An overpayment kept past the deadline is an obligation under the False Claims Act.

title: Florida Statutes 408.7057: Statewide provider and health plan claim dispute resolution program
note: Covers state-regulated insurers, HMOs and Medicaid prepaid plans. Excludes Medicare appeals, plans not regulated by the state and interest disputes. File within 12 months of the final determination.

title: Florida Statutes 409.908: Reimbursement of Medicaid providers
note: Subsection (13): Medicaid pays no part of Medicare deductibles and coinsurance when Medicare's payment equals or exceeds the Medicaid rate.

title: Florida Statutes 456.0625: Patient overpayments; refunds
note: Refund within 30 days after determining that the patient overpaid. A violation is grounds for discipline. Added by chapter 2025-48.

title: Florida Statutes 559.72: Prohibited practices generally (Florida Consumer Collection Practices Act)
note: Applies to any person collecting consumer debts, including an original creditor.

title: Florida Statutes 717.102: Property presumed abandoned; general rule
note: Dormancy period is 5 years unless another period is specified.

title: Florida Statutes 717.117: Holder due diligence and report of abandoned property
note: Written notice to the owner 90 to 180 days before reporting for property of $50 or more. Report before May 1 each year.

title: Revenue Cycle Management and Revenue Calculations (presentation to an HFMA chapter, November 2021)
note: Hospital scorecard targets: clean claim rate 85% or more, billed receivables over 90 days 20% or less, net denial write-offs 1.5% or less of net revenue, bad debt 2% or less of gross revenue. Based on PwC, HFMA, MGMA and HARA data. Not practice data.

title: Not-so-graceful aging: half of practices saw days in A/R increase in 2021 (MGMA Stat)
note: Quotes the 2021 MGMA DataDive Cost and Revenue median for receivables over 120 days in multispecialty practices: 13.54%.

title: What internal controls actually catch embezzlement in physician practices
note: The person who collects payments should not also post adjustments and reconcile the bank account. Article dated April 26, 2026. Only the public part was read.

title: Ask the Experts: Timely filing measurement
note: No industry standard known. One hospital respondent put timely filing at probably less than 1% of denial dollars.

title: Rate of initial denials of medical insurance claims continued to rise in 2024, Kodiak Solutions' proprietary data show (press release, syndicated copy)
note: Vendor data from more than 2,100 hospitals and 300,000 physicians. Providers collected 34.46% of amounts owed by insured patients in 2024, down from 37.58% in 2023.

title: Hospitals lost over $48B from claims denials, uncollected bills (report on Kodiak Solutions data)
note: Hospital medians: final denial rate 2.5% (2024) and 2.7% (2025), bad debt 1.1% and 1.3%. Overturn rate 42.1% in 2025. Secondary report of a vendor dataset.

title: Claims Denials and Appeals in ACA Marketplace Plans in 2024
note: 19% of in-network claims denied. Fewer than 1% of denied claims were appealed, and insurers upheld 66% of appeals.

title: 2026 UnitedHealthcare Care Provider Administrative Guide
note: One large insurer's manual, used as an example: rejected claims are not proof of timely filing, at least 90 days to file for participating commercial providers, disputes within 12 months of the remittance, virtual card payment when bank transfer is not set up.

title: A clean claim isn't a fully paid claim (2026 healthcare payments report card)
note: Vendor marketing based on 630 million professional claims: underpayments on 4.9% of claims, averaging 27% below the allowed amount. Method not published.

title: Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 30: Financial Liability Protections (Rev. 12934)
note: Advance Beneficiary Notice rules. The notice is for Original Medicare and is not used for Medicare Advantage.

title: 45 CFR 149.610: Good faith estimates for uninsured or self-pay individuals
42 CFR 424.502: Definitions (Medicare enrollment)
note: Authorized official, delegated official (an owner or W-2 managing employee), managing employee, and owner (5 percent or more direct or indirect ownership).

title: 42 CFR 483.10: Resident rights
note: Paragraph (d): the resident has the right to choose his or her attending physician. The facility may seek alternate physician participation if the chosen physician does not meet requirements.

title: 45 CFR 164.308: Administrative safeguards (HIPAA Security Rule)
note: Administrative safeguards of the HIPAA Security Rule. Paragraph (a)(1): risk analysis and risk management. Paragraph (a)(5): security awareness and training for every workforce member. Paragraph (a)(7): contingency plan with data backup, disaster recovery and emergency mode operation plans (required) and periodic testing and revision (addressable). Paragraph (b): written contracts with business associates. Unchanged as of November 6, 2026.

title: 26 CFR 1.1361-1: S corporation defined
note: Paragraph (l): one class of stock means all outstanding shares confer identical rights to distribution and liquidation proceeds under the governing provisions. Buy-sell agreements are generally disregarded.

title: HIPAA Security Rule To Strengthen the Cybersecurity of Electronic Protected Health Information (proposed rule, 90 FR 898)
note: Proposed 45 CFR 164.308(a)(13)(ii)(F): review and test contingency plans at least once every 12 months. A proposal only: not final as of November 2026.

title: Florida Statutes chapter 621: Professional service corporations and limited liability companies (sections 621.03, 621.09, 621.10, 621.11)
note: Shares may be issued or transferred only to licensed professionals or their professional entities. A disqualified owner must sever employment and financial interests forthwith.

title: File Annual Report
publisher: Florida Department of State, Division of Corporations
note: Annual report due by May 1. An entity that has not filed by the third Friday of September is administratively dissolved.

title: Practice Information: Corporate Practice of Medicine
note: Lists decisions a licensed physician must retain (including coding and billing procedures and payer contract parameters) and prohibited structures such as a medical practice run as a limited liability company.

title: Issue brief: Corporate Investors
note: States that the corporate practice of medicine doctrine varies widely by state and lists governance points for physicians dealing with corporate investors.

title: S corporation compensation and medical insurance issues
note: S corporations must pay reasonable compensation to shareholder-employees before non-wage distributions. The IRS may reclassify distributions as wages.

title: S corporations
note: Eligibility: domestic corporation, allowable shareholders only, no more than 100 shareholders, one class of stock. Election on Form 2553.

title: Beneficial Ownership Information Reporting
note: Final rule issued August 11, 2026 and effective August 14, 2026: US companies are exempt from beneficial ownership reporting.

title: Stay legally compliant
note: Corporations should hold annual meetings, record minutes, maintain bylaws and record stock transfers. Most states require an annual report or biennial statement. The address now redirects to the Manage your business guide.

title: Prepare for emergencies
note: Assess risk, create a plan, practice the plan with staff. A continuity plan should identify and document critical business functions. The address now redirects to the Manage your business guide.

title: Write your business plan
note: Traditional and lean plan formats. A lean plan is typically one page and can take as little as an hour. The address now redirects to the Plan your business guide.

title: Industry Segment-Specific Compliance Program Guidance for Skilled Nursing Facilities and Nursing Facilities
note: Physician arrangements such as medical directorships must reflect a real need, services actually provided, fair market value pay unrelated to referrals, and contemporaneous records such as time logs.

title: OIG Compliance Program for Individual and Small Group Physician Practices (65 FR 59434)
note: Physicians remain responsible for claims sent in their name by a billing service. Audits at least once a year: five or more records per federal payer or five to ten per physician. Medicare payments go to an account the provider controls.

title: AI Risk Management Framework: AI RMF Core
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
note: Voluntary framework. Govern function: inventory AI systems, document roles and responsibilities, define human oversight, leadership takes responsibility for AI risk decisions.

title: What is the difference between a compilation, review, and audit?
note: Compilation: no assurance. Review: limited assurance from inquiry and analytical procedures. Audit: the most assurance, with verification and substantiation.

title: Medical office embezzlement risk heightens at beginning of year
note: Reports an MGMA survey released November 5, 2010: nearly 83% of 688 practice managers had been affiliated with a practice where employee theft occurred. Describes concealment through write-offs and refunds.

title: Health leaders report they have 12-month strategic plans (MGMA Stat)
note: Poll of October 31, 2017, 1,212 applicable responses: 61% had a 12-month strategic plan, 34% did not, 4% unsure. Open poll, not a random sample.

title: Strategic plans can help guide medical groups in the short and long term (MGMA Stat)
note: 58% had a 12-month strategic plan, 37% did not, 5% unsure. Those with plans cite monthly financial statement review and quarterly progress checks.

title: The future of your medical group depends on who's ready when it matters most (MGMA Stat)
note: Poll of February 17, 2026, 302 applicable responses: 33% of medical groups have a succession plan for leadership positions, 60% do not, 8% unsure. 36% in July 2024.

title: Only 19% of practice leaders are very confident they could recover quickly from a cyberattack (MGMA Stat)
note: Poll of October 6, 2026, 238 applicable responses: 19% very confident, 61% somewhat, 21% not confident. Recommends a tabletop exercise twice a year. Notes 82% had a downtime plan in a July 2021 poll.

title: Survey: IT expenses per physician continue to rise to nearly $19,000
note: The most recent public MGMA figure found: $14,000 to $19,000 of technology operating expense per full-time physician in 2016.

title: Updated Special Advisory Bulletin on the Effect of Exclusion from Participation in Federal Health Care Programs
note: Issued May 8, 2013. No statute or regulation sets a screening frequency. The exclusion list is updated monthly, so screening employees and contractors each month best limits overpayment and penalty liability. Names billing and coding contractors and staffing agencies.

title: Health Care Fraud Self-Disclosure Protocol (updated October 15, 2026)
note: Not available for matters that involve only overpayments or errors, which go to the payer's voluntary refund process. Self-referral-only matters go to the CMS protocol. General practice: at least 1.5 times single damages. Minimum settlements of $20,000, or $100,000 for kickback matters. Samples of at least 100 items. Investigation findings due 90 days after the initial submission.

title: Health Care Fraud Self-Disclosure Protocol (web page with frequently asked questions)
note: Explains the four disclosure channels available in 2026 and states that items and services provided by unlicensed individuals are not payable by federal health care programs.

title: Justice Department's Civil Division and the Department of Health & Human Services Announce Anti-Fraud Healthcare Self-Disclosure Pilot Program
note: Press release of October 22, 2026. Six-month pilot for self-disclosing potential False Claims Act violations. Repayment with a 1.25 to 1.6 multiplier. Submissions accepted through April 22, 2027.

title: Corporate Integrity Agreement FAQ
note: Older agreements used a discovery sample of 50 paid claims, with a full sample and systems review if the net financial error rate reached 5 percent. Recent agreements review 100 claims with no threshold and require repayment of every overpayment found. Error rate is net overpayment divided by total dollars in the sample. Undated page, read November 10, 2026.

title: Targeted Probe and Educate
note: Contractors use data analysis to pick providers with high error rates or unusual billing, and services with high national error rates. Generally 20 to 40 claims a round, up to 3 rounds, then referral to CMS for possible 100 percent prepay review, extrapolation or referral to a recovery auditor. A low-volume version reviews fewer than 20 claims a round. Page last modified March 4, 2026.

title: Additional Documentation Request
note: Requests go to the practice address on file with Medicare, so the medical review correspondence address must be kept current. Best practice is to put the request letter on top of the response. Lists who reviews: Medicare Administrative Contractors, the Supplemental Medical Review Contractor, Recovery Audit Contractors and Unified Program Integrity Contractors. Page last modified March 4, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 405.903, 405.929 and 405.930: Prepayment review, post-payment review and failure to respond to an additional documentation request
note: 45 calendar days to answer a Medicare contractor and 30 to answer a Unified Program Integrity Contractor, with later acceptance for good cause. If the provider does not answer in time the contractor may deny the claim. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Medicare Fee-for-Service Compliance Programs
note: Describes medical review, recovery auditing and the Comparative Billing Report, which compares a provider's billing with peers in the state and nation. On November 2, 2026 the page said the reports were in development with release expected in late 2026 or early 2027.

title: CBR Guide - Part B
note: The Florida Medicare contractor's provider-specific comparative billing report is requested through its portal, and evaluation and management distribution reports are available on request. Peer comparison assumes each provider's specialty is reported accurately. Dated February 18, 2026.

title: Coding Trends of Medicare Evaluation and Management Services (OEI-04-10-00180)
note: From 2010 claims, flagged 1,669 physicians whose average visit level was in the top 1 percent of their specialty and who billed the two highest codes in a visit type at least 95 percent of the time.

title: Enforcement action: settlement of $41,739.66 for employing an excluded individual (Florida, January 6, 2025)
note: A podiatrist settled after an excluded receptionist provided items or services that were billed to federal health care programs.

title: 42 CFR 411.353: Prohibition on certain referrals by physicians and limitations on billing
note: No Medicare payment for a designated health service furnished under a prohibited referral, and amounts collected must be refunded. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 411.354: Financial relationship, compensation, and ownership or investment interest
note: Paragraph (e): a required writing may be a collection of documents, and a missing writing or signature can be obtained within 90 consecutive calendar days if the arrangement otherwise meets an exception. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: CPI-U Updates: annual limits for physician self-referral exceptions
note: For calendar year 2026 the nonmonetary compensation limit is $535 and the limit on limited remuneration to a physician is $6,237. Both are adjusted each calendar year. Page last modified February 19, 2026.

title: 42 U.S.C. 1320a-7b: Criminal penalties for acts involving Federal health care programs (Anti-Kickback Statute)
note: Subsection (b): knowingly and willfully paying or receiving any remuneration, in cash or in kind, to induce or reward referrals of federal program business is a felony. Bona fide employees are excepted. Subsection (g): a claim resulting from a violation is a false claim. Subsection (h): actual knowledge of the statute is not required.

title: Florida Statutes 456.054: Kickbacks prohibited
note: Unlawful for any health care provider to offer, pay, solicit or receive a kickback for referring or soliciting patients. Not limited to government payers.

title: Florida Statutes 817.505: Patient brokering prohibited
note: Unlawful for any person to pay or receive any commission, bonus, rebate, kickback or bribe to induce patient referrals to or from a health care provider or facility.

title: 45 CFR 164.404 to 164.410: Breach notification to individuals, the media and the Secretary, and by a business associate
note: Notify individuals without unreasonable delay and within 60 calendar days of discovery. A breach known to a workforce member or agent is treated as known to the practice. Breaches of 500 or more: notify the Secretary at the same time and the media. Smaller breaches: log and report within 60 days after year end. Business associates must notify within 60 days. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.524: Access of individuals to protected health information
note: Act on a request within 30 days. One extension of up to 30 days with a written statement of the reason. Fees limited to copying labor, supplies, postage and an agreed summary. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.520: Notice of privacy practices for protected health information
note: A provider with a direct treatment relationship gives the notice no later than the first service, makes a good faith effort to get written acknowledgment, and posts it only if it has a physical service delivery site. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.530: Administrative requirements (privacy training and documentation)
note: Train each new workforce member within a reasonable time and anyone affected by a material policy change, and document the training. No annual interval is stated. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.504 and 164.314: Business associate contracts
note: Required contract terms: report unauthorized uses, security incidents and breaches, bind subcontractors to the same terms, support patient access, return or destroy data at termination where feasible, and allow termination for a material violation. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 164.312: Technical safeguards (HIPAA Security Rule)
note: Unique user identification is required. Audit controls are a standard. Automatic logoff and encryption are addressable. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 414.1375: Promoting Interoperability performance category (Merit-based Incentive Payment System)
note: To score in this category a clinician must report completing the Security Risk Analysis measure during the year in which the performance period occurs. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Unified Agenda entry, RIN 0945-AA22: HIPAA Security Rule to Strengthen the Cybersecurity of Electronic Protected Health Information
publisher: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs
note: The 2026 agenda lists the rule under Long-Term Actions. The only completed step is the proposed rule of January 6, 2025. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Security Risk Assessment Tool
publisher: Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT
note: Free downloadable tool (version 3.7) built with the HHS Office for Civil Rights for small and medium providers. Using it is neither required by nor a guarantee of compliance.

title: Florida Statutes 501.171: Security of confidential personal information
note: Notice to affected individuals no later than 30 days after determining a breach. Notice to the Department of Legal Affairs when 500 or more people in Florida are affected. A third-party agent must notify the covered entity within 10 days. A practice that gives notice as its federal regulator's rules require (for a medical practice, the HIPAA breach rule) is deemed to meet the Florida notice requirement, and must still send a timely copy to the Department of Legal Affairs when the breach is large enough to require one.

title: 42 CFR 1001.1901: Scope and effect of exclusion
note: No federal health care program payment for any item or service furnished by an excluded individual or entity, or at the direction or on the prescription of an excluded physician. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 1003.200: Basis for civil money penalties, assessments, and exclusions
note: Penalties may be imposed for arranging or contracting with a person the provider knows or should know is excluded, for knowing of an overpayment and not returning it, and for making a false record material to a claim. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 21 CFR 1301.13: Application for registration, time for application and expiration date (Drug Enforcement Administration)
note: Practitioner registration runs 3 years. Renewal may be filed no more than 60 days before expiration, and the agency emails a notice about 60 days ahead. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 410.75: Nurse practitioners' services
note: Medicare covers the services when the nurse practitioner works in collaboration with a physician as state law defines it, or under documented arrangements where state law is silent. The physician need not be present. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Florida Statutes 464.012: Licensure of advanced practice registered nurses; protocols
note: An advanced practice registered nurse works within an established protocol kept on site where the nurse practices, unless registered for autonomous practice under section 464.0123.

title: Florida Statutes 458.348 and 459.025: Formal supervisory relationships, standing orders, and established protocols; notice
note: A physician or osteopathic physician who enters a protocol with an advanced practice registered nurse must notify the board within 30 days, and again within 30 days of ending it. Both sections were read.

title: Florida Statutes 458.319, 459.008 and 464.013: Renewal of license
note: Medical, osteopathic and nursing licenses renew every two years. All three sections were read.

title: 42 CFR 493.37: Requirements for a certificate of waiver (clinical laboratory)
note: A certificate of waiver is valid for no more than 2 years. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Form Instructions: Advance Beneficiary Notice of Non-coverage (ABN), Form CMS-R-131
note: Deliver before the service with time to decide. The identification number field is optional and Medicare numbers and Social Security numbers should not appear on the notice. The patient must choose one option. The provider cannot bill a dual-eligible patient when the notice is delivered.

title: FFS ABN (Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage)
note: Issued to Original Medicare beneficiaries when payment is expected to be denied. Skilled nursing facilities use it for Part B services only. Page last modified July 17, 2026.

title: States with Telehealth Consent Requirements
note: Says most states have some telehealth-specific consent requirement in statute, rule or Medicaid policy, and that in Medicare the requirement is limited to communication technology-based service codes. Lists no reference for Florida. Entries updated through August 2026.

title: Florida Statutes 456.47: Use of telehealth to provide services
note: Telehealth services must be documented to the same standard as in-person services. The section contains no separate consent requirement.

title: 42 CFR 482.22: Condition of participation: Medical staff
note: The medical staff operates under bylaws, appraises its members periodically, and requires a history and physical no more than 30 days before or 24 hours after admission. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 482.24: Condition of participation: Medical record services
note: Entries must be dated, timed and authenticated. Orders must be authenticated promptly. Records must be completed within 30 days following discharge. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 483.45: Pharmacy services (long-term care facilities)
note: Monthly drug regimen review. The attending physician must document review of each reported irregularity and the action taken. As-needed psychotropic orders are limited to 14 days unless the prescriber documents a rationale, and as-needed antipsychotic orders cannot be renewed without evaluating the resident. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 483.75: Quality assurance and performance improvement (long-term care facilities)
note: The quality assessment and assurance committee includes the medical director or a designee and meets at least quarterly. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 424.20: Requirements for posthospital SNF care (certification and recertification)
note: Certification at admission or as soon after as practicable. First recertification by day 14, then at least every 30 days. Signed by a physician, or by a nurse practitioner, clinical nurse specialist or physician assistant with no direct or indirect employment relationship with the facility. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Florida Statutes 429.26: Appropriateness of placements; examinations of residents (assisted living)
note: Each resident must be examined by a physician, physician assistant or advanced practice registered nurse within 60 days before or 30 days after admission.

title: Florida Statutes 458.320 and 459.0085: Financial responsibility
note: Minimum professional liability coverage of $100,000 per claim and $300,000 aggregate, or $250,000 and $750,000 for physicians with hospital staff privileges, or an escrow account or letter of credit. A physician may go without under stated conditions and must then tell patients by sign or written statement. Both sections were read.

title: Is Your Insurance Keeping Pace with Your Practice? (Vital Signs)
note: Recommends regular insurance reviews and an annual conversation with an advisor as practices add staff, technology and risks. Written to promote the society's own insurance agency, so it is opinion, not data.

title: 29 CFR 2580.412-11: Amount of the fidelity bond for employee benefit plans
note: The bond must be at least 10 percent of the plan funds handled, with a minimum of $1,000, and need not exceed $500,000. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Florida Statutes 440.02: Definitions (workers' compensation)
note: Covered employment includes all private employments with four or more employees, or one or more in the construction industry.

title: 42 CFR 422.311: RADV audit dispute and appeal processes (Medicare Advantage)
note: CMS audits the diagnoses that plans submit for risk-adjusted payment and may extrapolate results for payment year 2018 and later. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 424.535: Revocation of enrollment in the Medicare program
note: Grounds include a pattern or practice of claims that fail Medicare requirements, failure to report changes or adverse actions on time, and failure to document or give access to documentation. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 405.378: Interest charges on overpayment and underpayments to providers, suppliers, and other entities
note: Interest accrues from the final determination for each full 30-day period that payment is delayed, and is waived if the overpayment is repaid within 30 days. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 411.355: General exceptions to the referral prohibition related to both ownership/investment and compensation (in-office ancillary services)
note: Paragraph (b): in-office ancillary services may be furnished personally by the referring physician, a member of the same group practice, or a supervised individual, so a solo physician can use the exception. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 411.352: Group practice (physician self-referral)
note: Paragraph (g): no group member is paid on the volume or value of his or her referrals. Paragraph (i): profit shares and productivity bonuses on personally performed work, including RVUs, are allowed. Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-06.

title: 29 CFR 1910.1030: Bloodborne pathogens
note: Written exposure control plan reviewed at least annually (paragraph (c)(1)). Training at initial assignment and at least annually (paragraph (g)(2)). Training records kept 3 years (paragraph (h)(2)). Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-06.

title: 29 CFR 778.211: Discretionary bonuses (overtime regular rate), read with 29 CFR 778.208
note: Bonuses promised in advance, including bonuses for quality and accuracy of work, production, attendance or staying employed, must be included in the regular rate used for overtime. Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-06.

title: 29 CFR 541.600: Amount of salary required (overtime exemption)
note: Exempt executive, administrative and professional employees must be paid on a salary basis at or above a federal weekly threshold ($684 a week in the text in effect November 6, 2026). The salary test does not apply to practicing physicians. Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-06.

title: Independent contractor (self-employed) or employee?
note: Common-law test in three groups: behavioral control, financial control and type of relationship. An employer with no reasonable basis for contractor treatment may be liable for employment taxes. Page last reviewed May 19, 2026.

title: Physician Demand Stabilizes Amid Rising Turnover for Recruitment Professionals, According to AAPPR Report
publisher: Association for Advancing Physician and Provider Recruitment, via PR Newswire
note: 2023 data from nearly 150 health organizations and more than 17,000 searches: median time from search launch to signed contract for physicians ranged from 77 to 228 days by specialty. The full report is paywalled.

title: Tseng, Kaplan, Richman, Shah, Schulman. Administrative costs associated with physician billing and insurance-related activities at an academic health care system. JAMA 319(7):691-697
note: Read as the PubMed abstract, PMID 29466590. Billing and insurance-related costs were 14.5% of professional revenue for primary care visits ($20.49 and 13 minutes a visit, including physician time), from 2016 to 2017 interviews at one academic system.

title: 45 CFR 149.420: Balance billing in cases of non-emergency services performed by nonparticipating providers at certain participating health care facilities
note: An out-of-network clinician at an in-network facility may not bill a commercially insured patient more than in-network cost sharing, unless the notice and consent rules are met.

title: Hyman, Litwack, Quallich, Schram, Skolarus, Modi. Turnover among early-career advanced practice clinicians. JAMA Network Open 8(5):e258638
note: Read as the open-access full text in PubMed Central, PMC12053513. Medicare billing files for 217,487 clinicians who first billed from 2010 to 2021: 14.4% moved practices within 1 year (nurse practitioners 14.4%, physician assistants 15.4%) and 29.8% within 3 years.

title: Calendar Year 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule Final Rule: Quality Payment Program Fact Sheet and Policy Comparison Table
note: Posted November 4, 2026. Threshold 75 points through the 2028 performance year. Scores of 18.75 or less take the full 9% cut. Traditional MIPS ends after the 2030 performance year. New core measure requirement, small practices exempt. Submission window for 2026 data: January 4 to March 31, 2027.

title: How MIPS Eligibility Is Determined (Quality Payment Program website)
note: Low-volume threshold ($90,000, 200 patients, 200 services), eligible clinician types, new Medicare enrollees excluded, preliminary and final eligibility released each December, group participation brings in clinicians exempt as individuals, qualifying participants in advanced payment models excluded. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Special Statuses (Quality Payment Program website)
note: Small practice (15 or fewer clinicians): 6 quality bonus points, one improvement activity, Part B claims reporting, no promoting interoperability reporting required. Facility-based scoring requires 75% of services in a hospital (place of service 21, 22 or 23). Read November 10, 2026.

title: Small Practices (Quality Payment Program website)
note: When promoting interoperability is reweighted for a small practice: quality 40%, cost 30%, improvement activities 30%. A qualifying submission (all required data, measures and attestations) voids the automatic reweighting. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Exception Applications (Quality Payment Program website)
note: Extreme and uncontrollable circumstances and promoting interoperability hardship applications are due December 31, 2026, 8 p.m. Eastern. Small practices are reweighted automatically and need not apply. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Traditional MIPS overview and quality requirements (Quality Payment Program website)
note: Report by March 31 of the following year. The adjustment applies in the year after submission. Six quality measures and 75% data completeness are on the quality requirements page under the same path. Read November 10, 2026.

title: MVP Registration (Quality Payment Program website)
note: 2026 registration window for MIPS Value Pathways: April 1 to November 30, 2026. Read November 10, 2026.

title: 2025 MIPS Performance Feedback FAQs
note: Posted September 21, 2026, updated October 29, 2026. About 60 days to request a targeted review. The 2025 window closes November 30, 2026. Payment adjustment information follows about a month after final scores.

title: 42 CFR 414.1305: Definitions (Merit-based Incentive Payment System)
note: Low-volume threshold and small practice definitions. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: MIPS quality measures and historical benchmarks for the 2026 performance year (qpp-measures-data)
note: CMS open data repository behind the Quality Payment Program website. Benchmarks built from 2024 data: measure 047 (advance care plan) registry average 82.98%, median 99.13%. Measure 238 (high-risk medications, two or more orders in one class) electronic record average 4.79%. Measure text read from measures/2026/measures-data.json in the same repository.

title: 2026 Medicare pay: check your remittance advices
note: Positive MIPS adjustments appear with claim adjustment reason code 144, negative with 237, and remark code N807 may accompany either.

title: Medicare Managed Care Manual, Chapter 7: Risk Adjustment (Rev. 118)
note: Section 40: every diagnosis submitted must be documented in the medical record as the result of a face-to-face visit. Acceptable sources are hospital inpatient, hospital outpatient and physician services.

title: Announcement of Calendar Year 2027 Medicare Advantage Capitation Rates and Part C and Part D Payment Policies
note: April 6, 2026. 2027 payment uses diagnoses from 2026 dates of service. The 2024 risk model is kept for 2027. Diagnoses from audio-only visits and from chart reviews not linked to a visit are excluded. Video visits meet the face-to-face requirement.

title: 2026 Midyear Final ICD-10-CM Mappings (risk adjustment model software)
note: 8,019 diagnosis codes count in the 2026 payment model by our count of the file. Essential hypertension (I10), hyperlipidemia (E78.5), coronary disease without angina (I25.10) and history of stroke (Z86.73) do not. Acute stroke (I63.9) does.

title: Medicare Risk Adjustment Model CPT/HCPCS Filtering Included List, Calendar Year 2026
note: Nursing facility visit codes 99304 to 99310 and home or residence visit codes 99341 to 99350 are on the included list, as are office visits.

title: CMS Potentially Overpaid Medicare Advantage Organizations $462 Million Based on Certain Unsupported Acute Stroke Diagnosis Codes (A-02-23-01020)
note: Issued May 28, 2026. For all 97 sampled enrollees the acute stroke codes on physician records were not supported. Estimated $462 million for 2021.

title: Medicare Advantage Provider Complete Health to Pay $14,100,000 to Settle False Claims Act Suit
note: August 3, 2026. A provider organization paid under risk-sharing contracts settled allegations that it caused false diagnosis codes to be submitted.

title: 42 CFR 425.605: Calculation of shared savings and losses under the BASIC track
note: Paragraph (a)(1): CMS adjusts an organization's spending benchmark with prospective risk scores, with a cap on growth. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 425.110: Number of ACO professionals and beneficiaries
note: An accountable care organization must have at least 5,000 assigned beneficiaries. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 425.600: Selection of risk model
note: BASIC track glide path: levels A and B are one-sided (savings only), levels C to E share losses too. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 425.20: Definitions (Medicare Shared Savings Program)
note: An ACO participant is an entity identified by a Medicare-enrolled billing tax identification number. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: LEAD (Long-term Enhanced ACO Design) Model
note: Successor to ACO REACH, which ends December 31, 2026. Runs January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2036. Aimed at small, independent and rural practices and high-needs patients. Page last modified November 6, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 422.2: Definitions (Medicare Advantage)
note: Institutional special needs plans enroll people who live, or are expected to live, 90 days or longer in a long-term care facility, or who need that level of care. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: Medicare 2027 Part C and D Star Ratings Technical Notes
note: Updated November 4, 2026. Cut points from 2025 data. Blood pressure control 84% (4 stars) and 90% (5 stars). Transitions of care 69% and 80%. Readmissions 8% or less for 5 stars. Medication review for special needs plans 96% and 99%. Eight measures exclude members 66 and over living long-term in an institution.

title: 42 CFR 483.80: Infection control (long-term care facilities)
note: Paragraph (d): the facility must offer each resident influenza and pneumococcal immunization and document it. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: Yadav KN, Gabler NB, Cooney E, et al. Approximately One In Three US Adults Completes Any Type Of Advance Directive For End-Of-Life Care. Health Affairs 2017;36(7):1244-1251
note: Systematic review of 150 studies published 2011 to 2016 covering 795,909 people: 36.7% had completed an advance directive (38.2% of patients with chronic illness). Abstract read through PubMed.

title: American Geriatrics Society 2023 updated AGS Beers Criteria for potentially inappropriate medication use in older adults. J Am Geriatr Soc 2023;71(7):2052-2081
note: Applies to adults 65 and older in all ambulatory, acute and institutional settings except hospice and end-of-life care. Abstract read through PubMed.

title: Bindman AB, Cox DF. Changes in Health Care Costs and Mortality Associated With Transitional Care Management Services After a Discharge Among Medicare Beneficiaries. JAMA Intern Med 2018;178(9):1165-1171
note: Medicare claims 2013 to 2015, 18.8 million eligible discharges. Transitional care was billed after 7.0% of eligible discharges in 2015 and was associated with lower cost and mortality in days 31 to 60. Observational. Abstract read through PubMed.

title: Medicare Geographic Variation, by National, State and County (2014 to 2024)
note: National, Original Medicare, 2024: 224.8 inpatient stays per 1,000 beneficiaries (220.1 at 65 and over). All-cause 30-day readmission rate 18.07% (17.29%). Emergency visits 590.5 per 1,000. Read through the data.cms.gov API.

title: Nursing Home Chain Performance Measures, September 2026 release (national row)
note: National averages of Care Compare measures across 14,698 nursing homes: short-stay rehospitalization 23.7%, 1.9 hospitalizations per 1,000 long-stay resident days, long-stay antipsychotic use 15.4%, falls with major injury 3.2%, pressure ulcers 4.6%. Read through the data.cms.gov API.

title: Report to the Congress: Medicare Payment Policy, March 2026, Chapter 10: Hospice services
note: 2024: 52.9% of Medicare decedents used hospice. Lifetime length of stay among decedents: median 19 days, average 99.6, 5 days at the 25th percentile, 291 at the 90th.

title: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program
note: Payment reduction capped at 3% of base operating payments. Page last modified September 21, 2026.

title: Skilled Nursing Facility Value-Based Purchasing Program
note: CMS withholds 2% of skilled nursing facility Part A payments and returns 60% of the pool as incentives based on a readmission measure and others. Page last modified August 26, 2026.

title: Distribution of HCC Risk Scores, Calendar Years 2013 to 2024 (resource of the Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners by Provider dataset)
note: 2024, Original Medicare users of Part B services: average risk score 1.145, median 0.728, 75th percentile 1.28, 90th percentile 2.347.

title: Raffoul M, Moore M, Kamerow D, Bazemore A. A Primary Care Panel Size of 2500 Is neither Accurate nor Reasonable. J Am Board Fam Med 2016;29(4):496-499
publisher: Journal of the American Board of Family Medicine
note: Review from the Robert Graham Center: the often-quoted panel of 2,500 patients arose anecdotally with no research basis, and later studies found it infeasible. Abstract read through PubMed.

title: CAHPS Clinician and Group Survey Database: 2019 Chartbook
publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
note: Adult Survey 3.0 combined results from 2,002 practice sites and 330,390 respondents, surveys collected January 2019 to June 2020: access 65%, provider communication 85%, office staff 79%, care coordination 74%, provider rated 9 or 10 by 79%. Published October 2020.

title: HEAT Provider Compliance Training
note: Free video series (about four minutes each) and 16 webcast modules recorded May 18, 2011, covering fraud and abuse laws, compliance program basics, exclusions and documentation. Predates the 2025 change to the overpayment rule. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Types of Medical Malpractice Insurance Policies (fact sheet)
note: Occurrence policies cover events during the policy period whenever the claim is reported. Claims-made policies cover events on or after the retroactive date that are reported during the policy period. Gaps are closed by extended reporting (tail) coverage from the expiring insurer or prior acts (nose) coverage from the next one.

title: 29 CFR 2510.3-3: Employee benefit plan (plans without employees)
note: A plan that covers only a sole owner, an owner and spouse, or partners is not an employee benefit plan under title I of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, so the bonding rule reaches plans that cover employees. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Federal Register documents filed under RIN 0945-AA22 (HIPAA Security Rule update)
note: Queried November 10, 2026: the only document under this rulemaking number is the proposed rule of January 6, 2025 (document 2024-30983). No final rule had been published.

title: Medicare and Medicaid Programs; CY 2027 Payment Policies Under the Physician Fee Schedule (final rule, CMS-1848-F, 91 FR 70992)
note: Published November 9, 2026, effective January 1, 2027. Removes the Security Risk Analysis measure from the Promoting Interoperability category beginning with the 2027 performance period by amending 42 CFR 414.1375(b)(2)(ii)(A) to apply only through the 2028 payment year. States that the January 2025 HIPAA Security Rule proposal had not been finalized. Makes no change to 42 CFR 401.305, the self-referral rules or the nursing facility visit rules.

title: Work Plan
note: The work planning process is dynamic and projects are added through the year, so the list is not an annual document. Archives cover 1997 to 2024. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Targeted Probe and Educate (TPE) Q&As
note: Answer 9: the error percentage that counts as a high denial rate varies with the service under review and may vary by contractor, and moving to another round depends on improvement from round to round. The PDF carries no date in its text; its file was created May 24, 2018. Linked from the CMS program page. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Targeted Probe and Educate (presentation by National Government Services to an HFMA chapter, winter 2022)
publisher: National Government Services (Medicare Administrative Contractor), hosted by HFMA
note: One contractor's description of its own process, presented December 1, 2022 by its Part A outreach staff: a payment error rate under about 15% after a round ends the review, over about 15% leads to education and another round. Non-responses count as errors and the rate is not adjusted for appeal results. Slides, not policy, and may have changed. Read November 10, 2026.

title: QSO-22-15-NH & NLTC & LSC: Update to COVID-19 Emergency Declaration Blanket Waivers for Specific Providers
publisher: CMS Center for Clinical Standards and Quality
note: Memo of April 7, 2022. Ended, 30 days after publication, the waivers of 42 CFR 483.30 that had let nursing home physician visits be done by telehealth, let any required visit be delegated, and let physicians delegate tasks they must do personally. The in-person rule therefore comes from the facility regulation, apart from Medicare's telehealth payment limits. Read November 10, 2026.

title: 45 CFR 149.430 and 149.30: Provider and facility disclosure of patient protections against balance billing; definitions
note: A provider who furnishes services at a hospital, hospital outpatient department, critical access hospital or ambulatory surgical center must give commercially insured patients a one-page notice of balance billing protections, post it and put it on any website. The provider is covered if the facility does this under a written agreement. Providers who do not work at such facilities are exempt. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 2017 Healthcare Compliance and Auditing Survey Report
note: Vendor survey of compliance and auditing staff: 88% said their organization had a formal compliance program and 12% said it did not, and half of the 12% worked in small physician practices of 1 to 25 physicians. Self-selected respondents and old data, so it gives no rate for small practices. Read November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 455.410: Enrollment and screening of providers (Medicaid)
note: Paragraph (d): the state Medicaid agency must allow enrollment of all Medicare-enrolled providers and suppliers for processing claims for Medicare cost sharing, even for provider types the state does not otherwise recognize. Read through the eCFR API, November 10, 2026.

title: Claim scrubbing (product page)
note: Vendor marketing: guarantees a minimum 95% first-pass clean claim acceptance rate. Cited only as an example of where the 95% convention is repeated. No data given. Read November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 424.36: Signature requirements (Medicare claims)
note: The beneficiary signs the claim authorization. If the beneficiary cannot, a guardian, a relative who handles their affairs, or a representative of an institution that gave other care may sign. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 422.62: Election of coverage under an MA plan
note: Paragraph (a)(4): a person living in a long-term care facility may at any time join a Medicare Advantage plan, change plans or return to Original Medicare. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 423.38: Enrollment periods (Medicare Part D)
note: Paragraphs (c)(4) and (c)(35): people with the low-income subsidy may move into a stand-alone drug plan once a month, and full-benefit dually eligible people may move into an integrated plan once a month. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: Checking Medicare Eligibility (MLN8816413)
note: Fact sheet dated November 2025. A check needs the Medicare number, name and birth date. The answer shows Medicare Advantage plan, Medicare Secondary Payer, hospice and skilled nursing periods and Qualified Medicare Beneficiary status.

title: Getting MBIs: how providers get patients' Medicare Beneficiary Identifiers
note: The Medicare contractor's portal looks up a Medicare number from first name, last name, birth date and Social Security number. Page last modified September 10, 2024. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Top KPIs Physician Practices Should be Monitoring (white paper hosted by MGMA)
note: Vendor white paper. Source of the 98% insurance verification target, for which it cites a trade press article and no data.

title: CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F) fact sheet
note: Dated January 17, 2024. Medicare Advantage, Medicaid and CHIP payers must decide prior authorization requests in 72 hours (urgent) or seven calendar days (standard) and give a specific reason for denials, generally from January 1, 2026. Marketplace plans are excluded from the time limits. Drugs are excluded.

title: 42 CFR 422.568: Standard timeframes and notice requirements for organization determinations (Medicare Advantage)
note: Paragraph (b)(1)(ii): from January 1, 2026, seven calendar days for a standard request subject to the prior authorization rules. The plan may extend by up to 14 days in limited cases. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 422.572: Timeframes and notice requirements for expedited organization determinations (Medicare Advantage)
note: Paragraph (a)(1): an expedited decision is due no later than 72 hours after the request. Read through the eCFR API, text in effect November 6, 2026.

title: Prior Authorization and Pre-Claim Review Initiatives (Medicare fee-for-service)
note: Current Original Medicare programs: certain hospital outpatient department services, repetitive scheduled non-emergency ambulance transport, certain equipment and supplies, and review demonstrations. Page last modified September 15, 2025.

title: Submitting claims for Veteran care (Community Care)
note: All non-urgent and non-emergent care requires authorization from VA in advance. Emergency care can be authorized if VA is notified within 72 hours. Page last updated October 20, 2026.

title: Health Maintenance Organization (HMO) plans
note: In most HMO plans the member chooses a primary care doctor and in most cases needs a referral to use a specialist. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Sample Good Faith Estimate for Uninsured (or Self-Pay) Individuals
note: Revision dated August 2023. Shows the required content. Providers need not use this exact form if theirs includes the required information. The model notices are listed on the CMS No Surprises resources page.

title: What is Considered "Health Insurance"? Determining When Uninsured (or Self-Pay) Good Faith Estimate Rules Apply
note: File dated December 2024. No estimate is required for services scheduled fewer than 3 business days ahead. People covered by Medicare, Medicaid or another federal program are not entitled to an estimate, even for services the program does not cover.

title: Publication 538 (rev. January 2022), Accounting Periods and Methods
note: Who may use the cash method: S corporations and sole proprietors may. C corporations may if they meet the gross receipts test ($26 million, indexed for inflation) or are qualified personal service corporations, which include health services.

title: Open a business bank account
note: Business banking keeps business funds separate from personal funds and offers limited personal liability protection. A business account usually comes with the option of a line of credit.

title: Metric of the Month: Cycle Time for Monthly Close
note: APQC General Accounting Open Standards Benchmarking: of 2,300 organizations, median 6.4 calendar days from running the trial balance to finished consolidated statements. Top quarter 4.8 days or less, bottom quarter 10 or more. Not specific to medical practices.

title: Making Your Balance Sheet Work for You (Family Practice Management, June 2001)
note: Current ratio equals current assets over current liabilities. Banks consider about 2 to 1 the gold standard. Cash-basis balance sheets list no receivables. Banks treat loans from owners as equity, not liabilities.

title: Five financial ratios that track your practice's financial health
note: Current ratio, days in receivables, operating margin, working capital and days in payables. A current ratio under 1 means more is due within a year than the practice can turn into cash. One physician's guidance, no data.

title: Physician practice owners need to review key financial data points regularly
note: Owners should read the income statement, balance sheet and cash flow statement together. A current ratio above 1 shows the ability to pay debts due within a year. Written by a CPA and an attorney, no data.

title: Cash is King: Flows, Balances, and Buffer Days. Evidence from 600,000 Small Businesses
note: 597,000 small businesses with Chase accounts, February to October 2015. Median cash buffer 27 days of outflows (25th percentile 13, 75th percentile 62). Health care services median 30 days. Not limited to physician practices.

title: Physicians struggle to keep practices afloat after Change cyberattack (press release and survey summary)
note: Informal convenience survey, March 26 to April 3, 2024, more than 1,400 respondents, 78% from practices of 10 or fewer physicians. 80% lost revenue from unpaid claims, 55% used personal funds, 31% could not make payroll.

title: 42 CFR 405.371 and 405.372: Suspension, offset, and recoupment of Medicare payments; proceeding for suspension of payment
note: Medicare may suspend payments in whole or in part on reliable information that an overpayment exists or payments may not be correct, or on a credible allegation of fraud. Suspension is limited to 180 days with one extension of up to 180 days. The limits do not apply in fraud cases.

title: 13 CFR 120.160: Loan conditions (personal guarantees)
note: Holders of at least a 20 percent ownership interest generally must guarantee an SBA business loan. Text read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 13 CFR 120.214: What conditions apply for variable interest rates?
note: Maximum variable rates on 7(a) loans over the base rate (prime or the optional peg rate): 6.5 points for $50,000 or less, 6.0 up to $250,000, 4.5 up to $350,000, 3.0 above $350,000. No balloon payments.

title: H.15 Selected Interest Rates (Daily), release of November 9, 2026
publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
note: Bank prime loan rate 7.00% for November 2 to 6, 2026. The rate changes, so read the current release.

title: Paying yourself
note: A loan from a corporation to an officer should have a contract with a stated interest rate, a repayment period and a consequence for failure to repay. Below-market loans may be treated as wages or dividends. Partners are not employees. Page reviewed May 8, 2026.

title: 26 CFR 1.162-7: Compensation for personal services
note: Compensation is deductible only if reasonable and paid purely for services. An ostensible salary paid by a corporation with few shareholders may be a distribution of a dividend.

title: Estimated taxes
note: Sole proprietors, partners and S corporation shareholders generally must pay estimated tax if they expect to owe $1,000 or more. Four payment periods a year. A penalty can apply to a late or short payment. Page reviewed September 25, 2026.

title: Employment taxes and the Trust Fund Recovery Penalty (TFRP)
note: A responsible person who willfully fails to pay withheld taxes is personally liable for the unpaid balance. Paying other creditors instead is an indication of willfulness. Page reviewed October 11, 2026.

title: The 12-Step Way To Reduce Practice Expenses: Part 1, Staffing Efficiencies (Family Practice Management, March/April 2010)
note: Reprints MGMA Cost Survey for Single-Specialty Practices (2008 data): median operating expenses of family medicine practices not owned by hospitals were 59.74% of revenue, with support staff salaries 26.28% and benefits 5.52%. Excludes nonphysician provider pay (3.81%).

title: 9 ways to trim practice overhead without cutting patient care
note: States that MGMA puts total overhead at roughly 60% of practice revenue in a typical year. Trade press attribution, no table or data year given.

title: Kaplan RS, Porter ME. How to solve the cost crisis in health care. Harvard Business Review 2011;89(9):46-52
note: Argues that providers rarely know what care costs and sets out time-driven activity-based costing: cost each service by the time of the people and resources it uses. Abstract read through PubMed (PMID 21939127).

title: Occupational Fraud 2026: A Report to the Nations
note: 2,402 cases from 143 countries investigated since January 2024. Median loss $104,000 and 12 months to detection. 43% detected by tips. Primary weakness: lack of internal controls 33%, override 19%, lack of management review 18%. Health care: 140 cases, median loss $100,000. Not specific to medical practices.

title: Understanding Deposit Insurance
note: Deposit insurance covers $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, for each account ownership category. Corporation and partnership accounts are one category.

title: Revenue growth narrows as costs climb: the 2026 squeeze on medical practices (MGMA Stat)
note: Poll of June 30, 2026, 221 applicable responses: 47% of medical groups reported year-to-date revenue higher than the same period of 2025, 14% about the same, 36% lower, 2% unsure. A poll the week before found 84% with higher year-to-date costs. June 2025: 56% higher, 30% lower. Open poll, not a random sample.

title: Form CMS-855B: Medicare Enrollment Application, Clinics/Group Practices and Other Suppliers (version 12/2025)
note: Section 4A: report each practice location where services are rendered, including hospitals, retirement or assisted living communities and other health care facilities. Section 4D: areas served by home visits. Locations in another contractor's jurisdiction need a separate application. Form CMS-855I (05/23), section 4B, says the same for individual clinicians. Read November 10, 2026.

title: More than half of practices report credentialing-related denials on the rise in 2021 (MGMA Stat)
note: Poll of August 24, 2021, 425 responses: 54% saw credentialing denials rise. Some payers took as much as 100 days to give an effective date and allowed no retroactive claims.

title: 45 CFR 164.508: Uses and disclosures for which an authorization is required
note: Paragraph (a)(3): a covered entity must obtain an authorization for any use or disclosure of protected health information for marketing, except a face-to-face communication or a promotional gift of nominal value. Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-05.

title: 42 CFR 1003.110 and 1003.1000: Civil money penalties, definition of remuneration and beneficiary inducement
note: Remuneration includes waiver of coinsurance and deductibles unless the waiver is not advertised, not routine, and follows a good-faith finding of financial need or a failure to collect after reasonable collection efforts. Section 1003.1000(a) sets the penalty for inducing beneficiaries. Read in the eCFR version of November 6, 2026.

title: 42 U.S.C. 300gg-115: Protecting patients and improving the accuracy of provider directory information
note: Subsection (a)(2): group health plans and insurers must verify and update provider directory information at least every 90 days, set a procedure to remove providers they cannot verify, and post updates within 2 business days of receiving them.

title: 42 U.S.C. 300gg-139: Provider requirements to protect patients and improve the accuracy of provider directory information
note: Since January 1, 2022 each provider must have business processes to send plans directory information when a network agreement starts or ends, when the information materially changes, and on request.

title: Online Provider Directory Review Report (third round, November 2017 to July 2018)
note: Of 10,504 locations listed in 52 Medicare Advantage organizations' online directories, 48.74% had at least one inaccuracy. Earlier rounds: 45.10% (2016) and 55.07% (2016 to 2017). Methods changed slightly between rounds.

title: Florida Statutes 458.331: Grounds for disciplinary action; action by the board and department
note: Subsection (1)(d): false, deceptive, or misleading advertising is a ground for discipline of a physician.

title: Office of Inspector General Policy Statement Regarding Gifts of Nominal Value To Medicare and Medicaid Beneficiaries
note: December 7, 2016: nominal value means a retail value of no more than $15 per item or $75 in total per patient a year, never cash or cash equivalents. Gifts at or below these limits need not fit an exception to the beneficiary inducement penalty. Raised from $10 and $50 set in 2000.

title: 42 CFR 425.306: Participant agreement and exclusivity of ACO participants
note: Paragraph (b)(2): each participant (a billing tax identification number) that submits claims for services used to assign patients must be exclusive to one Shared Savings Program accountable care organization. Text read through the eCFR API, version dated 2026-11-06.

title: Medicare Shared Savings Program Accountable Care Organizations: Updated Performance Year 2024 Financial and Quality Results (fact sheet)
note: September 29, 2025. Of 476 organizations, 75% earned performance payments totaling $4.1 billion and Medicare saved $2.5 billion. Low revenue organizations, typically physician-led, saved $319 per person net against $180 for high revenue, typically hospital-led, ones. 16 owed shared losses totaling $20.0 million.

title: Financial buyer's side due diligence checklist: hospital acquisitions of physician practices
note: Four-page checklist: 47 checkbox items in 14 topics (10 on assets and liabilities, 4 on operations). The document is undated; PDF metadata shows it was created January 29, 2010, and the URL shows it was posted to the site in March 2021. The shared sources file lists it under slug pya-checklist with year 2021.

title: 5 Fundamentals for a Physician Practice Valuation
publisher: VMG Health (published by Becker's Hospital Review)
note: Names the three accepted approaches: income, market and cost. Page metadata gives the publication date as May 9, 2012 (last modified 2024). The shared sources file lists the same page under slug vmg-fundamentals with year 2024.

title: Healthcare Bulletin: State-Level Healthcare Transaction Notice Requirements and Their Impact on Practice Sales
note: Law firm bulletin dated July 1, 2025. Lists 18 states that require advance notice of health care transactions to state authorities, covering asset and equity sales of practices. Filing is due 30 to 180 days before closing. Most laws apply only above a revenue or price threshold. Florida is not on the list.

title: State health care transaction legislation in 2026: What passed, failed, and comes next
note: Law firm review dated October 24, 2026. California, Illinois, Maine, Washington, Connecticut and Vermont enacted or expanded transaction notice, review or ownership rules in 2026. Proposals in Colorado, Maryland, Hawaii, Rhode Island, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania and Indiana were not enacted.

title: Gottlieb, Shapiro, Dunn. The Complexity Of Billing And Paying For Physician Care. Health Affairs 37(4):619-626 (PubMed abstract, PMID 29608348)
note: Remittance data 2013 to 2015: fee-for-service Medicaid's claim denial rate was 17.8 percentage points above fee-for-service Medicare's, Medicaid managed care 6 points above, private insurance similar to Medicare Advantage.

title: Medicare Advantage in 2026: Enrollment Update and Key Trends
note: 55% of eligible beneficiaries (35.2 of 64.2 million) were in Medicare Advantage in 2026. Special needs plans hold 23% of that enrollment. Published June 5, 2026, updated July 1, 2026.

title: Physicians' Patient Mix: A Snapshot from the 2016 Benchmark Survey (Policy Research Perspectives)
note: Average patient shares in 2016: commercial 43.4%, Medicare 29.3%, Medicaid 16.9%, uninsured 6.1%. Shares of patients, not of revenue.

title: Florida Statutes 641.315: Provider contracts (health maintenance organizations)
note: 60 days' written notice to cancel, by either side. The organization must disclose its complete schedule of reimbursements and give 30 calendar days' written notice of changes. It may not require a practitioner to accept its other products.

title: Private Practice Toolkit: Payor Contracting 101
note: Payer types, what to weigh before joining a network, and contract basics. Notes that employer self-funded (ERISA) plans are usually exempt from state insurance laws such as prompt-pay laws.

title: Private Practice Toolkit: Payor Contract Review Checklist
note: Questions to ask of each clause: products, rates and their Medicare basis, payment deadlines, offsets, amendments, automatic renewal, termination without cause (for example 30 to 90 days' written notice).

title: Report to the Congress: Medicare Payment Policy, March 2026, Chapter 4: Physician and other health professional services
note: Preferred provider organization rates of one large national insurer averaged 147% of fee-for-service Medicare for clinician services in 2024 (140% in 2023, 122% in 2011): 124% for care management and coordination visits, 213% for CT scans.

title: Trish, Ginsburg, Gascue, Joyce. Physician Reimbursement in Medicare Advantage Compared With Traditional Medicare and Commercial Health Insurance. JAMA Intern Med 177(9):1287-1295 (PubMed abstract, PMID 28692718)
note: Claims of one large national insurer, 2007 to 2012: Medicare Advantage paid 96.9% of traditional Medicare for office visit 99213, and 91.3% to 102.3% across common physician services.

title: Roberts, Chernew, McWilliams. Market Share Matters: Evidence Of Insurer And Provider Bargaining Over Prices. Health Affairs 36(1):141-148 (PubMed abstract, PMID 28069857)
note: Office visit prices for small practices were $88, $72 and $70 as insurer market share rose, against $97, $86 and $76 for large provider groups.

title: Medicaid-to-Medicare Fee Index (State Health Facts)
publisher: KFF, from Urban Institute survey data
note: 2024: United States 0.75 for all services and 0.66 for primary care. Florida 0.64 and 0.56. Fee-for-service Medicaid physician fees only. 2019 figures were 0.72 and 0.67.

title: 45 CFR 147.212: Transparency in coverage, requirements for public disclosure
note: Group health plans and insurers in the individual and group markets must publish in-network rates in machine-readable files, for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2022. Grandfathered plans are exempt.

title: Arizona v. Maricopa County Medical Society, 457 U.S. 332 (1982)
publisher: U.S. Supreme Court, text at Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
note: Fee agreements among competing physicians are price fixing, unlawful in itself under section 1 of the Sherman Act. Joint ventures that pool capital and share risk are treated as a single firm.

title: 42 CFR 424.515: Requirements for reporting changes and updates to, and the periodic revalidation of, Medicare enrollment information
note: Revalidate every 5 years. Submit the application within 60 calendar days of the notice.

title: Revalidations (Renewing Your Enrollment)
note: Due dates are posted seven months ahead on the Medicare Revalidation List. Notices go out about three to four months before the due date. No extensions. No payment for services while deactivated. Page last modified July 29, 2025.

title: Form CMS-855I: Medicare Enrollment Application, Physicians and Non-Physician Practitioners (05/23)
note: Section 4: the practice location is where services are rendered. Clinicians who work in a hospital, retirement or assisted living community or other facility list those facilities. House-call-only clinicians may give a home address for administration. Reassignment is reported on this form.

title: 42 CFR 422.204: Provider selection and credentialing (Medicare Advantage)
note: Paragraph (b)(2)(ii): recredentialing at least every 3 years.

title: 42 CFR 455.414: Revalidation of enrollment (Medicaid)
note: The state Medicaid agency must revalidate every provider's enrollment at least every 5 years.

title: 42 CFR 422.214: Special rules for services furnished by noncontract providers (Medicare Advantage)
note: A clinician with no contract must accept, as payment in full, what could be collected if the patient were in original Medicare.

title: Annual Medicare Participation Announcement
note: Participation decisions run from mid-November through December 31. Medicare pays non-participating clinicians 5% less, and they may charge no more than 115% of the non-participating fee schedule amount.

title: New Special Enrollment Periods for Dually Eligible and Extra Help-eligible Individuals (job aid)
note: From January 1, 2025: a once-per-month election into Original Medicare with a stand-alone drug plan, and a once-per-month election into an integrated dual-eligible plan. Replaces the quarterly period.

title: Provider Payment Dispute Resolution for Non-Contracted Providers
note: Plans must pay non-contract providers no less than Original Medicare would pay, and those providers must accept it as payment in full. Page last modified September 10, 2024.

title: Data Book: Beneficiaries Dually Eligible for Medicare and Medicaid (December 2025)
note: Calendar 2022: 13.6 million dually eligible people, 20% of the Medicare population and 36% of Medicare spending. 11% lived in an institution, against 2% of other Medicare beneficiaries.

title: Florida Statutes 409.967: Managed care plan accountability (Medicaid)
note: Paragraph (2)(j): Medicaid managed care plans must comply with sections 641.315, 641.3155 and 641.513, the HMO contract and prompt-payment laws.

title: Florida Statutes 409.978: Long-term care managed care program
note: The state pays for Medicaid long-term care, including home and community-based services, through a managed care model.

title: Medicare Program Integrity Manual, Chapter 13: Local Coverage Determinations (Rev. 863)
note: Under section 1862(l)(5)(D) of the Social Security Act a contractor must post a final local coverage determination at least 45 days before it takes effect, after a proposed version and public comment.

title: MLN Connects Newsletter
note: Weekly national fee-for-service news for providers, suppliers, billers and coders, with an archive.

title: ICD-10 codes
note: New diagnosis codes take effect each October 1, with a further update each April 1. The October 1, 2026 files were posted when read.

title: File a Claim for Veteran Care (information for providers)
note: All non-urgent and non-emergency care needs authorization from the department in advance. The referral (VA Form 10-7080) says where to send the claim: Optum for regions 1 to 3, TriWest for regions 4 and 5.

title: 38 U.S.C. 1703D: Prompt payment standard (Veterans Affairs community care)
publisher: U.S. Code, text at Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
note: Subsection (b): claims must be submitted within 180 days of the service. Subsection (a): clean electronic claims paid within 30 calendar days, paper within 45.

title: 38 CFR 17.4035: Payment rates (Veterans Community Care Program)
note: Except as the section provides, payment rates will not exceed the applicable Medicare rate.

title: 32 CFR 199.7: Claims submission, review, and payment (TRICARE)
note: Paragraph (d): claims must be filed no later than one year after the services are provided.

title: 32 CFR 199.8: Double coverage (TRICARE)
note: Paragraph (d)(1): for a beneficiary eligible for both, Medicare is always the primary payer, except after a retroactive disability determination.

title: 45 CFR 149.30: Definitions (surprise billing rules)
note: For non-emergency services a health care facility is a hospital, a hospital outpatient department, a critical access hospital or an ambulatory surgical center.

title: Florida Statutes 627.64194: Coverage requirements for services provided by nonparticipating providers; payment collection limitations
note: Under state-regulated preferred and exclusive provider policies the insured owes a nonparticipating provider only cost sharing for emergency care, and for non-emergency care in a contracted facility when no participating provider could be chosen.

title: MGMA 2017 Cost and Revenue Survey (survey questions)
publisher: MGMA, copy hosted by the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology
note: Questionnaire only, no results. Operating cost lines include Legal Fees, Consulting Fees and Outside professional fees, so MGMA's paid cost survey holds a benchmark for these. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Measuring the rising costs of health IT compliance in medical groups (MGMA Stat)
note: March 16, 2023. Median technology cost per total relative value unit in the 2022 DataDive Cost and Revenue report: $0.57 for technology staff and $1.47 for technology operating cost, about 6% of the Medicare conversion factor. Also: $32,500 per physician in 2015 in physician-owned multispecialty groups, including equipment, staff and maintenance.

title: 45 CFR 170.315(b)(10): Electronic health information export (certification criterion for health IT)
note: A certified product must let a user export all of one patient's stored electronic health information at any time without developer assistance, and must support an export of the whole patient population, in a computable format. Read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026. Left in place by the final rule of October 28, 2026 (91 FR 67916).

title: 2025 CAQH Index: Executive Report
note: Free summary of the 2025 Index, which covers the year of the Change Healthcare attack. Medical provider average cost per transaction: $8.03 manual against $2.65 electronic ($7.93 and $3.39 in the 2024 Index). Transaction-level detail moved to a paid product. About one-quarter of providers reported using AI, mainly for administrative tasks.

title: 42 CFR 422.121 and 422.122: Provider access and prior authorization interfaces (Medicare Advantage)
note: Beginning January 1, 2027, a Medicare Advantage organization must maintain a Prior Authorization interface (422.122(b)) and a Provider Access interface (422.121(a)). Drugs are excluded. Read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: Medicare Claims Processing Manual, Chapter 24: General EDI and EDI Support Requirements, Electronic Claims, and Mandatory Electronic Filing of Medicare Claims (Rev. 13954)
note: Section 30.2, the electronic billing enrollment agreement. The provider agrees to be responsible for all Medicare claims submitted by itself, its employees or its agents, to tie every electronic entry to an original source document, to submit accurate claims, and to keep source documents and medical records at least 6 years and 3 months after the bill is paid.

title: Healthcare and Public Health Cybersecurity Performance Goals
publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services
note: Voluntary goals. The ten essential goals include email security, multifactor authentication, basic cybersecurity training, strong encryption, revoking credentials of departing workforce members, basic incident planning, unique credentials, separate user and privileged accounts, and vendor cybersecurity requirements. Read November 10, 2026.

title: Health Industry Cybersecurity Practices, Technical Volume 1: Cybersecurity Practices for Small Healthcare Organizations (2023 edition)
publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, 405(d) Program
note: Says smaller ambulatory practices are also targeted and can suffer greater proportional damage. Recommends unique accounts, role-based access, ending access as soon as a user leaves, and contract terms on return or destruction of patient data by technology vendors. Voluntary guidance.
