title: Testimony of the chief executive of UnitedHealth Group before the Senate Committee on Finance on the Change Healthcare cyberattack
note: May 1, 2024. On February 12, 2024 criminals used compromised credentials to reach a remote-access portal that did not have multi-factor authentication. Ransomware was deployed nine days later.

title: 45 CFR 171.302: Fees exception (information blocking)
note: The fees exception does not cover a fee to run the certified export of electronic health information for switching systems or giving patients their data, or a fee to export or convert data from health record technology that was not agreed in writing when the technology was acquired. Read through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026. Not changed by the final rule of October 28, 2026. Proposals of December 29, 2025 (90 FR 60970) to change other information blocking exceptions were still pending.

title: Change Healthcare cyberattack impact: key takeaways from informal AMA follow-up survey
note: Published April 29, 2024. Informal survey of April 19 to 24, 2024, 593 respondents, most from practices with fewer than 10 physicians. 75% still faced barriers with claim submission, 90% were losing revenue from unpaid claims, 62% were using personal funds and 34% could not make payroll. Of those who had not switched clearinghouse, 32% said their system did not support a switch.

title: Change Healthcare/Optum Payment Disruption (CHOPD) accelerated payments to Part A providers and advance payments to Part B suppliers (fact sheet)
note: March 9, 2024. Advance payments of up to 30 days of average Medicare claims payments, repaid by automatic recoupment from claims over 90 days, with a demand for any balance on day 91. A one-time program for that incident.

title: DOJ-HHS False Claims Act Working Group (press release 25-690)
note: July 2, 2025. Lists priority enforcement areas, including manipulation of electronic health record systems to drive inappropriate use of Medicare-covered products and services, and Medicare Advantage.

title: 2026 Provider Compensation and Productivity Data Report (2025 data)
note: Median total compensation for primary care physicians, 2025 data: $383,275 with supervisory duties and $322,865 without. By plan type: $345,852 on production-based plans and $314,404 on other plans. Median encounters in physician-owned primary care: 3,144.

title: Medical practices: a BV Rx
note: November 2005. For medical practices, market-data multiples are weak evidence and income-approach methods are the main basis of value. Understating reasonable physician compensation overstates goodwill.

title: Sale of a business
note: When a business is sold, each asset is treated as sold separately to figure gain or loss. Buyer and seller use the residual method to split the price among the assets. Page reviewed February 10, 2026.

title: Private Equity: Current and emerging financial due diligence considerations when acquiring physician practices
note: Advisory firm paper. A buyer has to settle how receivables and payables (working capital) are treated after the closing.

title: 26 U.S.C. 1366: Pass-thru of items to shareholders
note: Subsection (b): each item passed through to a shareholder of an S corporation keeps the character it had for the corporation.

title: 26 U.S.C. 1374: Tax imposed on certain built-in gains
note: A corporate-level tax on built-in gains an S corporation recognizes during the recognition period. Subsection (d)(7): that period is the 5 years beginning with the first day of the first tax year as an S corporation. Subsection (c)(1): the tax does not apply to a corporation that has always been an S corporation.

title: Florida Administrative Code 59A-4.1075: Medical Director (minimum standards for nursing homes)
publisher: Florida Department of State (Agency for Health Care Administration rule)
note: Effective May 5, 2026. From January 1, 2026 a nursing home's medical director must hold a medical director certification or be working toward one; a director appointed before that date has until December 31, 2028. The director must visit the facility at least once a month and document each visit, meet at least quarterly with the facility's risk management and quality committee, keep a principal office within 60 miles, and serve no more than 10 nursing homes.

title: Florida Administrative Code 59A-4.107: Physician Services (minimum standards for nursing homes)
publisher: Florida Department of State (Agency for Health Care Administration rule)
note: Effective May 5, 2026. Paragraph (6): each resident must be seen by a physician or another licensed health professional at least once every 30 days for the first 90 days after admission and at least once every 60 days after that. A visit is timely if it is made within 10 days of the date it was required. Paragraph (7): a physician may designate another health care professional to carry out the physician's part of resident care after the required visit.

title: 42 CFR 405.928: Effect of the initial determination
note: Paragraph (b): a Medicare contractor's first decision on a claim is binding on all parties unless a redetermination (the first level of appeal) is completed or the decision is revised through a reopening under section 405.980. Text from the copy the reviewers saved through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 438.602: State responsibilities (Medicaid managed care program integrity)
note: Paragraph (b): the State must screen, enroll and periodically revalidate every network provider of a Medicaid managed care plan. A plan may sign a network agreement while enrollment is pending, for up to 120 days, but must end it at once when the State says the provider cannot be enrolled or when the 120 days pass without enrollment. Text from the copy the reviewers saved through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 414.1320: MIPS performance period (Merit-based Incentive Payment System)
note: Paragraph (e): quality and cost are measured over the full calendar year, January 1 through December 31, two years before the payment year. Improvement activities need at least 90 days in a row within that calendar year. Text from the copy the reviewers saved through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 414.1325: Data submission requirements (Merit-based Incentive Payment System)
note: Paragraph (e): data are due by March 31 after the performance period closes, or a later date CMS sets. Quality reported on Medicare Part B claims must be on claims with dates of service inside the performance period. Paragraph (b)(1): claims reporting of quality is for small practices only. Text from the copy the reviewers saved through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: 42 CFR 414.1380: Scoring (Merit-based Incentive Payment System)
note: Paragraph (c)(2): beginning with the 2024 payment year the electronic-records category (Promoting Interoperability) is reweighted for a clinician in a small practice. Paragraph (e): a clinician who furnishes 75% or more of covered professional services in inpatient hospital, on-campus outpatient hospital or emergency room settings is facility-based and is scored on the hospital's results for quality and cost. An individual clinician scored that way has no data to submit. Text from the copy the reviewers saved through the eCFR API on November 10, 2026.

title: The SPOT User Guide: Section 6 - Appeals
note: How to ask the Florida Medicare contractor to reopen a paid claim through its online portal. A reopening may be requested for any reason within one year of receipt of the initial determination, and in writing with good cause up to four years. On a Part B claim line the dates of service, place of service, procedure code and modifiers can be edited. Page dated September 30, 2026.

title: Florida Statutes 90.507: Waiver of privilege by voluntary disclosure
note: Florida Evidence Code. A person who holds a privilege, such as the lawyer-client privilege in section 90.502, waives it by voluntarily disclosing, or consenting to the disclosure of, any significant part of the confidential matter or communication. Federal privilege law would govern a federal case.

title: 42 U.S.C. 1395nn: Limitation on certain physician referrals (physician self-referral law)
note: Subsection (g): Medicare may not pay for a designated health service furnished on a prohibited referral, and amounts collected for it must be refunded. A person who bills for a service that he knows or should know is barred faces a civil money penalty of up to $15,000 for each service.

title: Calendar Year 2027 Physician Fee Schedule Final Rule Addenda (CMS-1848-F), updated November 5, 2026
note: Addendum B gives the 2027 relative values by code: nursing facility visit 99309 has practice expense 1.30 in both settings, and complex care management 99487 has 2.38 non-facility and 0.42 facility. Addendum E gives the geographic indices: Rest of Florida work 0.977, practice expense 0.971, malpractice 1.54. Its note says the 1.0 floor on the work index was extended through January 1, 2027, so the 2027 work indices do not reflect it. Used with the 2027 conversion factor of 32.6286 to price the practice's codes for 2027. Read from the copy the reviewers saved on November 10, 2026.
